title: fix(release): refuse a Version Packages PR whose queue build lands behind main; mark next.2's 11 missed changesets
body:
Fixes #23818

Clause-②: no

## What this PR does

This PR is the guard half of #23818. The changeset half was split out to #23835.

1. **A merge-time guard.** `node scripts/release-pending-publish.mjs queue-guard --event EVENT --base SHA --head SHA` judges a merge-queue build. It exits 1 when the Version Packages PR in that build was cut from a base that `main`, or a queue entry ahead of it, has since passed by at least one changeset.
2. **Its wiring.** One step in `lint.yml`'s `Lint · CI, release & engine gates` lane (`lint-ci-engine`, behind the required `Lint & Repo Gates`) runs the guard on every build. It judges only a `merge_group` build, the one CI run that sees the tree that lands.
3. **The 11 next.2 entries are split out to #23835.** That PR carries `Part of #23818` and is not governed. It lands first, so the next.3 Version Packages PR can be refreshed without waiting for this Tier H approval. Until then, this branch still carries the same 11 lead lines (commit `15f51d126`). Once #23835 lands, this branch merges `main` and those hunks drop out. That merge was measured clean ahead of time (see "The split" below).

**Tier H.** The diff touches `.github/workflows/lint.yml`. `check-governed-merges --branch` reads 1 of 13 paths governed, landing tier H (人合). This PR lands only with the maintainer's hand or an authorised APPROVED review.

## Root cause: why #21373's guard did not catch next.2

#21373 added `release-pending-publish.mjs unconsumed`. `release.yml`'s `release-integrity` job runs it in the push that carries the version commit, on the branch where `select` answers `pending: true` (that push lands the version commit, and the version is not on npm yet).
- It lists every top-level `.changeset/*.md` in the version commit's tree that `pre.json` does not record as consumed.
- It reports them as a `::warning::` and a job-summary section.
- Its header states the contract: "The report never refuses a release."

On next.2 it measured correctly. Run 38841989023 (the push of `e5136ff10f`, 02:44Z) carried the warning `11 changeset(s) from 10 commit(s) are still in the tree of the version commit e5136ff10f ...`, naming all 11. The publish job started at 02:47:48Z.

The case it misses is about **timing, not pre mode**:
- **It runs after the landing.** By then the CHANGELOG.md files are already written into the version commit that the publish ships. By contract it only warns.
- **Nothing before the landing judges the tree that lands.**
  - A `pull_request` build cannot do it. A scheduled refresh starts no `pull_request` build at all: #23825's head `d5c44f86be` has 0 check runs. A dispatched refresh does start one: #23481's head `958e5b07b7` has 45, with the maintainer as triggering actor. Either way, that build judges the PR against the base it was cut from, where it is current by construction.
  - Only the merge-queue build sees the tree that lands, and until this PR none of its steps read changesets.
- **Pre mode played no part.** In pre mode, @changesets/cli v3 moves what a prerelease pass consumes into `.changeset/pre/`, and `pre.json` keeps no list of ids. So the top-level read is correct in pre mode, and it did name all 11.

The card's premises, checked against a full-history clone (`git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` answers `false`):
- **Ancestry.** For each of the 11, the commit that added it passes `merge-base --is-ancestor` against `e5136ff10f` (exit 0). Against the PR's base `4fe8b3def0` it fails (exit 1). Control leg: root commit against `4fe8b3def0` gives exit 0.
- **Not consumed.** None of the 11 is under `.changeset/pre/` at `e5136ff10f`.
- **No CHANGELOG entry.** No `## 18.0.0-next.2` CHANGELOG section names any of them. `packages/spec`'s section (763 lines) has 0 lines naming `full-width`.

## The guard

It lives in `scripts/release-pending-publish.mjs` as the new mode `queue-guard`, next to `unconsumed`. It calls the same `unconsumedChangesets`, so the two modes cannot disagree about what "unconsumed" means.

On a `merge_group` build it does three things:
1. It walks the first-parent commits of `base..head`. `base` and `head` are the payload's `merge_group.base_sha` and `merge_group.head_sha`; the base already includes every queue entry ahead of this one.
2. It finds each version commit in that range, using `select`'s definition: the CLI version differs from the first parent's.
3. It measures the unconsumed changesets **at that commit**, not at the build's head. A later entry's changeset in the same batch belongs to the next release, so it is not counted.

The verdicts:
- `behind`: exit 1, with an `::error::` that names each changeset and the commit that added it. The remedy it prints is to refresh the Version Packages PR from the current main (dispatch `release.yml` with `refresh_version_pr: true`, the bookkeeping lane only) and queue it again with no changeset-bearing PR ahead of it.
- `current`: exit 0.
- `no-version-commit`: exit 0. Every ordinary build gets this, so no ordinary PR depends on the guard.
- Any event other than `merge_group`: exit 0, saying it is not a merge-queue build.
- Refused, never guessed: a `merge_group` build without a full base **and** head sha (a ref name such as `HEAD` is refused too), a base that is not an ancestor of the head, or a shallow clone.

### Proof

**Self-test.** `node scripts/release-pending-publish.mjs --self-test` passes 113 cases across 28 batteries (it had 22). There are six new batteries:
- the next.2 shape in v3 pre-mode layout, refused, naming exactly the late changesets; the CLI exits 1;
- a cut refreshed from the current main passes (the control), and the stale PR is also current against its own base;
- a build that moves no version is never judged;
- a batch is judged at its version commit, never at the batch head;
- the non-pre shape is refused too;
- another event, plus every refusal: an empty, short, missing or foreign base; an empty head or a ref-name head; a shallow clone. For the empty base and the empty head, the refusal is also pinned through the CLI.

**The miss, reproduced as a control in the self-test.** On the same fixture, the post-landing `unconsumed` report names the same three late changesets and answers only a `::warning::`.

**Ablation (round 1).** I committed the guard first, then used `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` to disable the `behind` branch, with a trap that restores the file. The anchor hit once (1 -> 0). The self-test went red on 5 cases. Restore: the blob equals HEAD and `git diff HEAD` is empty.

**Real history.** I ran the guard read-only, from this branch's script, in a full-history clone. The local commits in this table were never pushed.

| build | base | head | exit | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| #23481 (next.2) queue build | `8684079f2a` (its parent) | `e5136ff10f` | 1 | refused: 11 changesets from 10 commits, the card's exact list |
| #23825 (next.3), squashed onto main `1ecb08a1c` | `1ecb08a1c` | `0f5edbbbbd` (local squash) | 1 | refused: `23731-activity-changed-fields` (#23814) and `23808-type-descriptions-plain` (#23817) |
| #23825 against its own base | `f606ba2e25` | `d5c44f86be` | 0 | current |
| next.3 cut from this branch (local `changeset version`) | `15f51d126` | `c078e7c25a` (local) | 0 | current |
| an ordinary landing | `43567a8fcb` | `0cfd0c49bd` | 0 | no version commit |

A version build takes 0.13 s and an ordinary one 0.07 s.

## The wiring

The step sits in `lint-ci-engine`, right after `Release version-commit selection self-test`. That puts it at lines 3331-3352 of `lint.yml`, about 700 lines away from #23824's hunk (`@@ -4057`) in the same job.

```yaml
      - name: Version Packages PR lands no changeset behind main
        id: version-packages-pr-lands-no-changeset-behind-main
        continue-on-error: true
        env:
          OS_GATE_EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
          OS_GATE_MERGE_GROUP_BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.merge_group.base_sha }}
          OS_GATE_MERGE_GROUP_HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.merge_group.head_sha }}
        run: node scripts/release-pending-publish.mjs queue-guard --event "$OS_GATE_EVENT_NAME" --base "$OS_GATE_MERGE_GROUP_BASE_SHA" --head "$OS_GATE_MERGE_GROUP_HEAD_SHA"
```

It carries a rationale comment and follows the lane's conventions: an `id`, `continue-on-error: true`, and the GATE INVOCATION IDIOM (`node scripts/...`).

### Each claim, proved against the edited `lint.yml`

**(a) The lane verdict reads the step, with no roster edit.** `scripts/ci/lane-verdict.mjs` builds its roster from the workflow: every step of the job with `continue-on-error`. I parsed the edited `lint.yml` with its own `laneSteps`. The result is 67 steps and 60 gates, and the new step is at position 15 with `gate=true`, its id set, and no `if:`. I then ran the real verdict (`GITHUB_JOB=lint-ci-engine`) on three `steps` contexts:

| context | exit | verdict line |
|---|---|---|
| all green | 0 | `ok       Version Packages PR lands no changeset behind main`; `OK -- 60 gate(s): 60 passed` |
| new step `outcome: failure`, `conclusion: success` | 1 | `RED      Version Packages PR lands no changeset behind main -- outcome failure`; `FAILED -- 60 gate(s): 59 passed, 1 red` |
| new step absent from the context | 1 | `UNREAD   Version Packages PR lands no changeset behind main`; `1 unread` |

**(b) On `pull_request` and `push` it answers "not a merge-queue build" and exits 0.** I ran the step's literal `run:` line, read out of the parsed workflow, with the environment GitHub renders on those events (the `merge_group` fields are empty). Each event exits 0 with this line:

`Version-PR queue guard: event pull_request is not a merge-queue build, and only a merge_group build lands a commit on main, so there is nothing to judge here.`

The same holds for `push`, `schedule` and `workflow_dispatch`.

**(c) On `merge_group`, base and head come from the payload and are never guessed.** The parsed `env` maps to `${{ github.event.merge_group.base_sha }}` and `${{ github.event.merge_group.head_sha }}`. I ran the same `run:` line in a full-history clone of this head:

| input | exit | answer |
|---|---|---|
| the #23481 queue build's base and head | 1 | refused: 11 changesets |
| an ordinary landing | 0 | no version commit |
| empty head | 1 | `needs --head, the group's full head sha (got "")` |
| `HEAD` as the head | 1 | `needs --head ... (got "HEAD")` |
| empty base | 1 | `needs --base ...` |
| short base `8684079f2a` | 1 | `needs --base ... (got "8684079f2a")` |

**(d) The lane's checkout gives a non-shallow clone.** The parsed checkout step is `actions/checkout@v7` with `fetch-depth: 0`, which fetches all history. The lane already resolves `github.event.merge_group.base_sha` on queue builds: its issue-citation step depends on it, and `lint.yml` records that measurement. The guard is also fail-closed on depth: it refuses a shallow clone with a named reason, so a shallow checkout would turn this step red and never green. Reading a live queue run's checkout log is NOT MEASURED: the job-log blob answers 403 from this container.

**Workflow lint.** `actionlint` 1.7.7 (release tarball, sha256 `023070a287...0757`, matching its published checksums) gives exit 0 with 0 findings on the edited `lint.yml`, and also 0 on the base version. shellcheck is not installed, so actionlint's `run:`-script pass was skipped. The repo's own linters `check:workflow-status-functions` and `check:workflow-step-name-quoting` both exit 0.

## The split (#23835) and the coming merge

- **What #23835 carries.** It is a cherry-pick of `15f51d126` onto `43567a8fc`, and its `git patch-id --stable` is identical (`36811cbc07`). Its own derived gates: 20 families, 19 exit 0, and the expected foreign-changeset refusal.
- **The merge, measured.** I squashed #23835 onto main `0cfd0c49bd` (local, never pushed) and merged that into this branch's head `31e38ea07` with `git merge-tree`. It exits 0 with no conflict. Against that simulated main, this PR then carries 2 files: `.github/workflows/lint.yml` (+22) and `scripts/release-pending-publish.mjs` (+359 / -2). The 11 changeset hunks are gone.
- **Changed lines.** Today this PR is 405 changed lines (+403 / -2) over 13 files. After that merge it is 383 lines (+381 / -2) over 2 files.

## What to do about #23825 (next.3) now

**Hold it.** Do not queue it as it stands.
- It is behind main by two changesets (#23814, #23817), and once this guard is wired it refuses that queue build (table above).
- Its next.3 CHANGELOG renders the 11 without the lead line.
- Once #23835 lands, #23825 conflicts: it moves the 11 files into `.changeset/pre/`, and #23835 edits them in place.

**Then refresh it once, after #23835 lands.** Dispatch `release.yml` with `refresh_version_pr: true` alone (the fleet relay's refresh stroke). That re-cuts next.3 from the then-current main, so it consumes the 11 with their lead lines plus everything since.

**Then queue it.** Until this PR lands, nothing refuses a stale queue build, so queue it only with no changeset-bearing PR ahead of it. After this PR lands, the guard refuses one.

## Acceptance notes

None of these is filed; each is polish or an inference, not a defect class.
- **ADR-0087 pass line.** `check-adr-0087-registration`'s pass line counts inherited-breaking changesets as "non-breaking": `11 non-breaking changeset(s) seen`, where 4 of the 11 declare breaking. This is misleading wording only, and the verdict is right.
- **Inheritance exemption.** The same exemption means a PR that edits an already-breaking changeset is not asked for its ADR-0087 disposition again, so deleting its marker would pass. This is read off the code and was not exercised.
- **The post-landing remedy.** `unconsumed`'s post-landing warning prescribes "Name them in the VERSION release notes". With this guard wired, that warning is only the backstop for a merge that bypasses the queue, which runs no `merge_group` build.

## Local gates (final head `31e38ea07`)

- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 68 families. Touching `lint.yml` added 27 to round 1's 41. Each was run with its exit code captured before any pipe.
  - **67 exit 0.** These include:
    - `release-pending-publish.mjs --self-test` (113 cases / 28 batteries);
    - `check-aggregator-roster`, `check-step-collectors`, `check:required-contexts`, `check:select-gate-families`, `check-self-test-wired` and `check-self-test-workflow-commands`;
    - `check:workflow-status-functions` and `check:workflow-step-name-quoting`;
    - `check:type-check-coverage`, and `check:type-check-debt` (`--re-measure`, 294.5 s under the verify lock);
    - `check:pm-governed-merges`, `check-adr-0087-registration --base`, `check:nul-bytes`;
    - `pnpm check:pm-dispatch-gates` (fast tier, 1884 cases).
  - **1 exits 1, as expected:** `check-empty-changeset.mjs --base origin/main`. It refuses the 11 `M` rows this branch still carries until #23835 lands and `main` is merged. #23835's body carries the deliberate-correction confirmation.
- **Reconciliation:** `--ran` reports 68 derived, 68 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED.
- **Lint:** `eslint --no-inline-config scripts/release-pending-publish.mjs` exits 0. `actionlint` 1.7.7 on `lint.yml` exits 0 with 0 findings.
- **Governance:** `check-governed-merges --branch` reports 1 of 13 paths governed (`.github/workflows/lint.yml`), landing tier H, 405 changed lines (+403 / -2).

## 维护者速读(草稿)

**改了什么**
发版流程加了一道"合并队列关卡"。版本合并请求(Version Packages PR)进入合并队列时,系统会检查:这次要发布的版本,是否漏掉了在它生成之后才合入主干的变更说明。如果漏了,就拒绝合入,并提示先刷新版本合并请求,再重新排队。普通合并请求不受影响。
那 11 条"已在 18.0.0-next.2 发布、但更新日志漏记"的补记,已拆到 #23835 单独先合。

**为什么改**
18.0.0-next.2 的版本合并请求是在主干又合入了 11 条变更之后才合并的。这 11 条变更的代码随 next.2 发了出去,但 next.2 的更新日志里没有记。其中有破坏性变更:升级到 next.2 的用户在更新日志里查不到,hotcrm 升级时校验直接失败。
原来的检查只在发版之后提醒,不会拦截。当前待合的 next.3 版本合并请求(#23825)已经又落后主干 2 条,如果照原样合并,会再漏一次。

**风险与代价(含回滚)**
- 代价:版本合并请求必须在"它前面没有带变更说明的合并请求"时排队,否则会被退回,需要先刷新再排队。合入节奏稍慢,但不会漏记。
- 风险:关卡只读 git 历史,不发布、不写入。对普通合并请求只输出"本次不涉及版本",耗时约 0.1 秒。
- 回滚:删掉 `lint.yml` 中新增的这一步即可,或整体回滚本合并请求;不影响任何已发布的版本。

**席位意见**

**你要做的**
1. 审阅并批准本合并请求(涉及工作流文件,属 Tier H)。
2. 先合入 #23835(不受管,可走普通队列)。合入后,在本合并请求上合并 main,那 11 条补记会从本合并请求的改动中消失。
3. #23835 合入后,刷新 #23825(next.3):以 `refresh_version_pr: true` 触发 `release.yml`。确认它前面没有带变更说明的合并请求后,再排队合并。
